summary: Google DeepMind announced the Fairwind Program, a limited-access initiative giving governments, enterprises and cybersecurity partners access to its Gemini 3.8 Flash Cyber model combined with the CodeMender harness to autonomously find, verify and fix software vulnerabilities.

mechanisms.reason: The program frames vulnerability remediation as autonomous, agent-executed work performed at scale across 650 partners rather than manual seat-based security work.
mechanisms.quote: The Fairwind Program offerings bring together our most advanced cyber model, Gemini 3.8 Flash Cyber , with our CodeMender harness, to help defenders find, verify, and fix vulnerabilities at agentic scale.

practices.reason: Engineers evaluating cyber-focused models would note the claimed combination of specialized vulnerability-fix reasoning with lower operating cost than general frontier models, though it is unreplicated and access-gated.
practices.quote: CodeMender with Gemini 3.8 Flash Cyber delivers the specialized reasoning to write and validate code fixes, at a fraction of the operating cost of traditional frontier models.

practices.reason: The CodeMender harness is named as the scaffolding that turns model output into verified, deployable patches, but the mechanism is not described in enough detail to implement independently.
practices.quote: Instead of taking weeks to manually fix vulnerabilities, defenders can now generate verified, deployment-ready patches in minutes — within an organization’s secure cloud environment.

practices.reason: Non-Fairwind customers can already reach similar capability generally via CodeMender on the Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform, which is a availability note rather than a required migration.
practices.quote: any Google Cloud customer can proactively secure their code by using CodeMender with publicly available models hosted on Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform, in combination with industry-leading solutions offered through AI Threat Defense
